name: Triodanis
look_here_first: Compare the leaf base, the flower, and the seed capsule opening.
shared_traits: Individual five-lobed flowers on alternate-leaved herbs
Closed and open flowers may coexist on one stem
Species require leaf bases and mature capsule, not just flower color
taxonomy_note: Triodanis biflora is accepted as Triodanis perfoliata subsp. biflora under Kew and ITIS.

genus_diagnostics.flower: One usually blue-violet five-lobed corolla, not an Asteraceae composite head; lower closed self-pollinating flowers can be present.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Simple alternate leaves, with broad clasping bases in typical perfoliata but narrower non-clasping or tapered bases in related taxa.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Inferior green many-seeded capsule with tiny side opening called a pore/window; position varies by taxon, often middle in typical perfoliata and nearer apex in biflora.
genus_diagnostics.stem: Leaf axils bearing upper open flowers and lower closed flowers; narrow ribbed stalks in coloradoensis and leptocarpa.

lookalikes.name: Lobelia
lookalikes.separator: Asymmetric two-lipped corolla and anther tube rather than regular-looking violet star and free stamens.

lookalikes.name: Asteraceae
lookalikes.separator: Composite flower head instead of one flower with five lobes.

visual_comparison.title: The leaf attachment and capsule window are the key
visual_comparison.subtitle: Four species plus one subspecies; verify exact photos and label unphotographed species as pending.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Clasping leaf + middle capsule window suggests typical perfoliata; less-clasping + tip window suggests biflora.
